newsitem.title: USA: NYC comptroller sets Tues. briefing on Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: NYC comptroller sets Tues. briefing on Swiss banks.

text.p: New York City Comptroller Alan Hevesi said Monday he plans to hold a briefing Tuesday about the outcome of his meetings last week with the heads of the three Swiss banks, Swiss government officials and leaders of the Swiss Jewish community.

The city comptroller last year asked the banks to explain how they were responding to probes of whether the banks blocked victims of the Holocaust and their survivors from withdrawing valuables they deposited in Switzerland for safekeeping.
Hevesi is a trustee and investment adviser to the city's $70 billion pension fund, which owns stock in the three Swiss banks, and the banks also handle investments for the city and pension funds.
The three Swiss banks that the city comptroller met with last week were Credit Suisse Group, Swiss Bank Corp and Union Bank of Switzerland, a spokesman for Hevesi said.

As of Dec 31, 1996, the city's pensions owned 262,800 shares of Credit Suisse, valued at nearly $26 million, 56,700 shares of Swiss Bank, which were worth almost $10.8 million, and 22,800 shares of Union Bank, which were pegged at about $13.3 million.

The New York City Council, which considered whether to require the city's pensions to divest themselves of Swiss banks' stocks, put the proposal on hold after the Swiss government in February created a fund for Holocaust victims.

The fund was set up to defuse the country's worst foreign policy crisis since World War II, which was sparked by allegations that Swiss banks hoarded unclaimed wealth of Holocaust victims and that neutral Switzerland cynically profited from the war.
